title: Map
description: A battlefield: a character grid plus named markers and zones. One character per tile — '.' open, '1'/'2'/'3' cover levels (light/heavy/garrison), 'r' road, 'o' olive grove, 'n' rocky knoll, '^' rock ridge (impassable, blocks sight), and any building symbol declared in data/structures.json. Authorable in a text editor on purpose: maps are the scatter-prop and sightline budget of a mission, and contributors should be able to sketch one without tooling. The loader (packages/data parseMap) additionally checks that row counts and lengths match the declared dimensions and that markers/zones are in bounds.

items.description: One character per tile. Terrain: "." open, "1"-"3" cover levels, "r" dirt road, "o" olive grove (cover 1), "n" rocky knoll (cover 2), "^" rock ridge (impassable, no cover, blocks line of sight -- the only blocked tile that is not a building, and therefore the only one with no HP, no garrison and no ROE penalty). Building symbols are whatever data/structures.json declares -- a contiguous run of identical building symbols is one structure. The pattern here is deliberately permissive: listing symbols in a regex meant they were hardcoded in three places at once, and validate_data.mjs now cross-checks every symbol against the structure catalogue and the terrain legend instead, so it cannot drift. A prior version of this pattern still hardcoded an alphanumeric-plus-# allowlist, which silently excluded punctuation symbols like the wall type's "=" -- the same drift the refactor was meant to prevent. Any single non-whitespace character is legal here; the catalogue and terrain legend are the only real authority on which ones mean something.

terrain.description: Terrain theme: which tone bundle and ground texture the renderer draws this map with. Presentation only -- it never reaches the sim, exactly like the decor layer. 'arid' is the Sahar limestone-and-dust look every map before Naharin uses; 'green' is the Naharin river basin. Adding a theme is a renderer change; adding a map that uses one is not.

elevation.description: Per-tile elevation, one digit 0-9 per tile, with the same dimensions as rows. Absent means every tile is height 0. Deliberately orthogonal to the terrain symbol: a symbol table can express ridges but not valleys, and elevation needs both. 0-4 is the practical authoring range -- deeper relief reads as a wall rather than as terrain -- but 0-9 is legal so a dramatic peak needs no format change.

markers.description: Named points missions reference: spawn anchors, tunnel mouths, HVT positions.

zones.description: Named rects [x, y, w, h]: objective areas, trigger regions, no-fire zones.

tunnels.description: Underground routes. Geometry lives here because it is terrain; a mission activates a route and stocks it, and a route no mission references does not exist that mission.

pre_dug.description: The route starts fully excavated: dig progress at full length, vent open. One of the two ways authored data opens a route -- the other is a mission placement whose digs field names it, excavating live and leaving spoil. No trail is stamped at load: spoil is what digging leaves behind, and a route finished before the mission began has weathered -- reveal it with mark_tunnel or the ledger.
